exec: // Authenticates every request. A bearer token (api_token) wins when set: the
// server ignores the session cookie if an Authorization header is present.
// Otherwise the session cookie from Log in is sent by Postman's cookie jar,
// and unsafe methods need the session's CSRF token.
// Every long-running operation returns 202 with the queued job.

request.description: Newest first, without live `runtime` state.

Queues provisioning in `client_group_id`. Saves the site's ID to `site_id` and the job's to `job_id`. Optional fields: `admin_username`, `php_version`, `resources` (`cpu`, `memory_reservation_mb`, `memory_limit_mb`).

Imports a site into `client_group_id` from a `wp-content` archive (`.tar.gz`, `.tar`, or `.zip`) and a SQL dump (`.sql` or `.sql.gz`), both sent first with **Uploads** (purpose `site_import`, same client group) and named here by `archive_upload_id` and `dump_upload_id`. The job checks both before it creates the site, so the site only exists once the job's `validate` step has passed. Saves the new site's ID to `site_id`. Optional fields: `name` (defaults to the imported site's title), `php_version`, `resources`.
Includes the live `runtime` state.
Changes `php_version`, `resources`, and/or `preview_protection`; a job recreates the affected containers. See **Turn on preview protection** for the preview password.

The first time, the platform generates the password and returns it in `preview_credentials` of this response **only**; the test saves it to `preview_username` and `preview_password`. Turning protection on again later reuses the same credentials and returns none. Add `"username"` to choose the username (default: the site's slug).

item.description: Site backups, restores, and backup schedules. A client group's sites share one Restic repository.

request.description: The site's backups, newest first, including running and failed ones. Saves the newest succeeded backup's `snapshot_id` to `snapshot_id`, for **Restore site**.

Queues a job that dumps the site's database and snapshots it with `wp-content` into the client group's backup repository (design doc §5.3). The job's result holds `backup_id` and `snapshot_id`. Follow it with **Jobs → Get job**, then **List site backups** saves the snapshot for **Restore site**. Needs `backup` configured and `task_image` set.

Queues a job that restores `snapshot_id` into the site (design doc §5.4), after taking a pre-restore backup (the job's result holds `pre_restore_backup_id`). The site must be `running`. To restore another site's snapshot from the same client group, add `source_site_id`. If the job fails after touching the site's data, it rolls back and leaves the site in maintenance mode.

request.description: When the site is backed up automatically and when its next backup is due. Every site is backed up daily by default, at a time within the platform's backup window.

Replaces the site's backup schedule; omitted fields take their defaults, so `{"enabled": true}` restores the daily backup in the platform's window. `interval_hours` is a divisor of 24 or a whole number of days up to 168; `hour` is the UTC hour backups start in, or `null` for the platform's window. Applies at once, without a job.

item.name: Core updates
item.description: WordPress core updates (design doc §5.5): minor and security releases roll out automatically, one site at a time; major releases wait for approval per site or client group; holds keep a site on its major branch. The image rollout moves sites to new builds of the images they run (PHP patch releases, security fixes, base OS updates) the same way, one site at a time.

request.description: The site's WordPress version, the release it moves to next, a pending major release, its and its group's policy, and warnings.
Keeps the site on its current major branch, which still gets its minor and security releases. `{}` makes it follow its client group again.
Lets the site move to the newest release of any branch up to `approved_branch`, which must have site images (`GET /api/v1/core-rollout`).
Queues the update to the site's next release now, outside the maintenance window. Returns 409 if there is none.
The policy the group's sites follow unless they have their own.
`{"hold": true}`, `{"approved_branch": "7.2"}`, or `{}` for the group's sites without a policy of their own.
The releases with site images, the maintenance window, failed site updates, and whether the rollout is halted.
Lifts a halt after repeated failures and queues a rollout pass.
The newest builds of the site images in use, the maintenance window, failed site updates, and whether the rollout is halted.
Lifts a halt after repeated failures and queues a rollout pass.

item.name: Uploads
item.description: Resumable uploads of large files for site imports and code deployments. Only the user who starts an upload can use it.

request.description: Starts a resumable upload for a site import into `client_group_id` (for a deployment, use `"purpose": "site_deploy"` and `"site_id"` instead). The sample declares the 11 bytes `hello world` that **Send chunk** sends; for a real file, declare its size and SHA-256 and send it with a file body. Saves the upload to `upload_id` and resets `upload_offset`.
Where the upload stands. After a failed chunk, resume from `received_bytes`, which this saves to `upload_offset`.
Sends the next chunk (at most 32 MiB) from `upload_offset`, and saves the new `received_bytes` to it. A chunk that fails counts for nothing; send it again.

Checks the content against the SHA-256 checksum given when the upload started (or pass `"sha256"` here) and makes the upload available to its import or deployment. On a mismatch the upload is removed (`422`).
Removes an upload that no job has taken.

item.name: Database
item.description: Access to a site's database without its password: exports to download, and temporary database sessions tunneled through the SFTP gateway (design doc §5.8).

request.description: Queues a job that dumps the site's database and compresses it with gzip. Follow it with **Jobs → Get job**, which saves the result's `export_id` for **Download database export**. The export can be downloaded until `expires_at` in the job's result (an hour by default, `database_export.ttl_seconds`); then it is deleted.

The compressed dump (`application/gzip`) of `export_id`; use **Send and Download** to save it. Import it with `gunzip < dump.sql.gz | mariadb mydb`. An expired or unknown export returns `404`. Every download is recorded in the audit log.

Creates a temporary MariaDB user limited to the site's database and returns its credentials, shown only once, with the `ssh -L` command for the tunnel through the SFTP gateway. Saves `db_session_id`, `db_session_username`, and `db_session_password`. `access` is `read_only` (the default) or `read_write` (Admins only); `ttl_seconds` runs from 60 to 28800, an hour by default. Run the `ssh_command` with a key registered on your account, then connect to `127.0.0.1:3307`.
The site's active database sessions, without passwords.
Ends `db_session_id` at once: its MariaDB user is dropped, its connections are ended, and the gateway refuses new tunnels for it. A session that has already ended returns `404`.

Follow it with **Jobs → Get job**.
